newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil reports progress in Chinese field.
newsitem.headline: Statoil reports progress in Chinese field.

text.p: Drilling of the first of five production wells on the Chinese Lufeng field in block 22-1 in the South China Sea was making good progress, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.
Drilling began in late November. All five wells are due to be drilled by May or June when they will be completed for oil production. The field is planned to come on stream in late 1997.
Statoil is cooperating with China's state-owned Chinese National Offshore Oil Co (CNOOC) in the development, which lies in an established oil province about 250 km (155 miles) off Hong Kong.
The field contains about 35 million barrels of oil -- less than in Statoil's Yme field, the smallest independent development on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Lufeng will be developed using a production vessel tied to a template on the seabed.
